pr_title: All hid_ops callbacks get device pointer.
pr_body:
This commit extends USB hid API callbacks by adding
'const struct device *dev' parameter. If the application
configured more than one HID device then it must specify
separate hid_ops for each device as its unable to determine
for which device the callback was called.

This patch makes it possible to have only one hid_ops within
the application and the application is aware for which device
the callback was called because of explicit device pointer.

Signed-off-by: Emil Obalski <emil.obalski@nordicsemi.no>

Fixes: #27612

issue_context.title: RFC: API Change: usb: Device argument to USB HID ops
issue_context.body:
**Problem description**
We need to support multiple instances of HID trough the USB. Each USB HID device gets ops. The problem is ops callbacks do not have the device pointer as an argument which makes it impossible to use single function for all devices and complicates application's code for no good reason.

**Proposed change**
Pass a device pointer along with a HID USB ops callback. An example:
```diff
-typedef void (*hid_int_ready_callback)(void);
+typedef void (*hid_int_ready_callback)(const struct device *dev);
```

**Dependencies**
usb HID samples under `./samples/subsys/usb/`

**Alternative**
The alternative is to create N functions and do some macro magic to assign them when registering HID USB devices in the for loop.
